newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money has easier bias at month end.
newsitem.headline: German call money has easier bias at month end.

text.p: German call money rates eased back to around 3.0 percent on Wednesday as average reserve levels remained ample.

Traders said the usual month-end rate of around 3.50 percent was unlikely to materialise, with expectations that deposit figures for the whole month, due later in the session, would confirm good liquidity.

"Every bank will know by early afternoon how the reserves stand," said one trader. "It is possible that until then, the Lombard facility will be used, but at the moment there is very little activity there."
Data from Tuesday showed that around 0.1 billion marks was borrowed on the Lombard, while daily bank deposits at the Bundesbank stood at 41.3 billion marks, up from 40.3 on Monday.
The average for the month was 41.1 billion marks, unchanged from the Monday's level.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average (FIONA) rate was quoted at 3.19667 percent in Wednesday's midsession trade, up from 3.0700 percent on Tuesday.
